page.layout: One column of text, with a woodcut initial P at the start of the first paragraph. Italic and black-letter headings stand between the paragraphs. Running head at the top above the text, page number above it. No marginal notes. The text ends with a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.head: Quid est Polemica?
main_text.p: POLEMICA, die kriegekunst / est ars bellum recte administrandi.
main_text.head: Quid est bellum?
main_text.p: Bellum est legitima poena, suscepta ab ordinaria potestate, propter justam causam, ad-versus sceleratos publicae pacis turbatores, seditio-sos & contumaces, propter hunc finem, ut publica pax, aut conservetur, aut recuperetur, & in pace vera doctrina de Deo, & aliae artes & linguae utiles & ne-cessariae propagentur.

p.bl: Der Krieg ist ein rechtmäßige straffe/von der verordneten Oberkeit geübet/umb gerechter sache willen / wider die boßhafftigen zer-störer gemeines frieden / vnd die aufrürischen/vnnd halßstarrigen/zu diesem ende/daß der gemeine friede entweder erhalten oder wider erlanget werde / vnnd daß im friede die wahre lehr von Gott / vnnd andere künste / vnd sprachen nützlich vnd nohtwendig erweitert werden.

main_text.head: In quibus versatur Polemica?
In quo est apparatus belli?
main_text.p: In legione, cohortibus legionis, Imperatoribus, Tribunis, centurionibus, militibus, civibus robustis & armorum peritis, in pilo, scuto, galea, lorica, manicis, ocreis, gladiis, hastis, tormentis, nummo, commeatu, & vestibus.

Doubtful: "Woh" in the heading "Woh in stehet die rüstung zum Krieg?" is read with some uncertainty; the "h" may be a ligature or a different word. The "ab•ordinaria" mark between "ab" and "ordinaria" is a printer's ornament or stop, transcribed as a space. The catchword "fen/" stands alone at the right below the last line. Show-through of the other side is visible at the right edge and was left out.
